column2: What is Gini impurity in decision trees?
column6: Gini impurity is a measure used in decision trees to evaluate the quality of splits. It quantifies how often a randomly chosen element from the set would be incorrectly labeled if it was randomly labeled according to the distribution of labels in the subset.

Stratified k-fold cross-validation involves dividing the dataset into k subsets or folds, where each fold has approximately the same proportion of classes as the original dataset. This ensures that each fold maintains the same distribution of classes as the entire dataset when evaluating the model's performance.
